chapter.heading: Peter Defends God’s Grace
chapter.v:
Now the
apostles and brethren who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God. [Acts 14:26] [Acts 11:22]

And when
Peter came up to Jerusalem, those of the circumcision contended with him, [Num. 8:14;]

saying, “You
went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them!” [Matt. 9:15;]

But Peter
explained it to them in order from the beginning, saying: [Acts 4:36]

“I was
in the city of Joppa praying; and in a trance I saw a vision, an object descending like a great sheet, let down from heaven by four corners; and it came to me. [[Acts 13:46]]

When I
observed it intently and considered, I saw four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, creeping things, and birds of the air. [Acts 8:9 1 NU]

And I
heard a voice saying to me, ‘Rise, Peter; kill and eat.’

But I
said, ‘Not so, Lord! For nothing common or unclean has at any time entered my mouth.’ [Ex. 7:11; 2 Tim.]

But the
voice answered me again from heaven, ‘What God has cleansed you must not call common.’ [Acts 2:4; 4:8]

Now this
was done three times, and all were drawn up again into heaven. [Matt. 13:38;]

At that
very moment, three men stood before the house where I was, having been sent to me from Caesarea. [Ex. 9:3;]

Then the
Spirit told me to go with them, doubting nothing. Moreover these six brethren accompanied me, and we entered the man’s house.

And he
told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house, who said to him, ‘Send men to Joppa, and call for Simon whose surname is Peter, [Acts 15:38]

who will
tell you words by which you and all your household will be saved.’ [Acts 16:13]

And as
I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, as upon us at the beginning. [Luke 4:16]

Then I
remembered the word of the Lord, how He said, ‘John indeed baptized with water, butyou shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’ [Acts 10:35]

If therefore
God gave them the same gift as He gave us when we believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could withstand God?” [Ex. 6:1, 6;]

When they
heard these things they became silent; and they glorified God, saying, “Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life.”Barnabas and Saul at Antioch [Ex. 16:35;]

Now those
who were scattered after the persecution that arose over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to no one but the Jews only. [Deut. 7:1]

But some
of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, preaching the Lord Jesus. [Judg. 2:16;]

And the
hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord. [1 Sam. 8:5]

Then news
of these things came to the ears of the church in Jerusalem, and they sent out Barnabas to go as far as Antioch. [1 Sam. 15:23,]

When he
came and had seen the grace of God, he was glad, and encouraged them all that with purpose of heart they should continue with the Lord. [Is. 11:1 #]

For he
was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a great many people were added to the Lord. [Matt. 3:1;]

Then Barnabas
departed for Tarsus to seek Saul. [Matt. 3:11;]

And when
he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. So it was that for a whole year they assembled with the church and taught a great many people. And the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.Relief to Judea [Ps. 66:16]

And in
these days prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch. [Luke 23:34]

Then one
of them, named Agabus, stood up and showed by the Spirit that there was going to be a great famine throughout all the world, which also happened in the days of Claudius Caesar. [Matt. 27:22,]

Then the
disciples, each according to his ability, determined to send relief to the brethren dwelling in Judea.

This they
also did, and sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.
